scenarios.name: stop_interrupts_long_answer
scenarios.description: Speaker prompts the bot ('tell me about yourself'), bot starts a long monologue, speaker says 'stop'. Bot MUST cut TTS within 500 ms of speech onset, MUST NOT emit any follow-up utterance.

assertions.name: all_expected_transcripts_persisted
assertions.detail: persisted=['Tell me about yourself.', 'Stop, please.']; expected_keywords=['tell', 'stop']; missing_keywords=[]

assertions.name: bot_started_speaking_before_interrupt
assertions.detail: no AgentSpoke published; the bot never reached TTS so an interrupt could not be measured. Likely the router did not approve speaking, or the LLM/TTS failed.

assertions.name: interrupt_to_cut_latency_budget
assertions.detail: could not determine interrupt-onset monotonic time or first AgentSpoke event

assertions.name: all_expected_transcripts_on_event_bus
assertions.detail: bus_texts=['Tell me about yourself.', 'Stop, please.']; missing_keywords=[]

scenarios.name: stt_keeps_running_during_bot_speech
scenarios.description: Reproduces the Johnny-har contract: participant speech mid-bot-utterance MUST land in the transcript sink. This is the regression that today's session-160 evidence proves is back — the 'stop' utterances never reached transcript_chunks at all.

assertions.name: all_expected_transcripts_persisted
assertions.detail: persisted=['Please describe the meeting bot architecture.', 'Just a side comment here.', 'And one more thing to add.']; expected_keywords=['please', 'just', 'more']; missing_keywords=[]

assertions.name: all_expected_transcripts_on_event_bus
assertions.detail: bus_texts=['Please describe the meeting bot architecture.', 'Just a side comment here.', 'And one more thing to add.']; missing_keywords=[]

transcripts_persisted: Please describe the meeting bot architecture.
And one more thing to add.

utterances_persisted.output_text: The meeting bot architecture typically includes several main components. First, there's an audio processing module that captures and transcribes spoken conversation into text. Next, natural language understanding components analyze this transcript to identify intents, topics, and action items. Dialogue management handles interactions with users, ensuring smooth conversational flow. A knowledge base or memory stores meeting context and past discussions for reference. Finally, integration with calendar and communication platforms allows the bot to join meetings and share summaries or action points. Together, these components enable the bot to effectively assist users during meetings by understanding and managing conversational content.

scenarios.name: cough_does_not_interrupt
scenarios.description: A short cough mid-bot-utterance MUST NOT trigger fast barge-in. VAD still finalises the cough as an utterance after the configured end_of_speech_ms silence; the classifier verdict is no-interrupt (category=noise) and the router declines to speak so the bot's answer completes in full.

utterances_persisted.output_text: Certainly! Additionally, it can help manage meeting agendas, track decisions, and generate follow-up tasks. If you'd like, I can provide more detailed information about any specific aspect of the system.
